topic: Myth: Applying for Finance Always Hurts Your Credit Score
objective: Correct a common misconception: 'Applying for Finance Always Hurts Your Credit Score'.

slides.headline: Myth: Applying for Finance Always Hurts Your Credit Score
slides.subheadline: The impact depends on how you apply.
slides.visual_concept: Premium editorial photograph: a business owner reviewing a credit report on a laptop, calm expression

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: A single, well-targeted application typically has a limited impact on your credit file. It's applying to many lenders in quick succession — not applying itself — that compounds the effect.

slides.headline: What's actually true
bullet_points: A single application has limited impact
Multiple rapid applications compound the effect
Some lenders offer pre-assessment without a full enquiry
Your file recovers over time regardless

caption:
This myth stops a lot of business owners from even making a well-considered enquiry — but the real risk comes from applying to multiple lenders at once, not from a single, well-matched application.
